title: How Much House Can You Afford by Salary? (5 Levels)
publish_for: 2026-11-26 L2 21:00 svensk tid (= 15:00 Eastern) – SATSNING_30D + KÖ_ÄNDRING_2026-11-26_DRIFT. 3 Shorts 27/11 10:07/14:07/18:07 via Studio i Chrome.
format: FORMAT_BLUEPRINT QM + serien 'How Much House/Car Can You Afford' (TILLÄGG 22 nov punkt 2): krok vid ett öppet hus ($416,700 NAR) → receptet på tavlan (28 %, 7,21 %, skatt, försäkring, 9 % insats, PMI) → 5 lönenivåer = BLS-percentiler 10/25/50/75/90 med dom per nivå → baklänges: lönen huset kräver → invändningar (Redfin, lägre ränta) → Paula mot Sam (36 %-linjen, $27,748) → dom → fråga. Ingen musik.

beats.text: Dom nivå 5: enda som klarar skylten

scenes.say: Saturday morning, an open house two streets over. Only one number matters.
The sign says 416,700 dollars, the October median for an existing home.

visual.label: median existing-home price, all housing types, Oct 2026 (National Association of Realtors)

scenes.say: So how much house can you afford by salary? Five pay levels will show us.
Your paycheck says 1,232 dollars a week, the typical full-time salary today.

visual.label: median weekly earnings, full-time workers, Q3 2026 (BLS)

scenes.say: Over 52 weeks that adds up to 64,064 dollars, or 5,339 a month before tax.
Lenders often start from a rule of thumb: housing should take at most 28 percent of that.
And here's the twist: only one of our five levels actually reaches that sign.
Two neighbors come along for the math. Payment Paula and Steady Sam both earn that same 64,064 dollars.
By the end, a car payment gap of just 205 dollars will move Paula's maximum house by almost 28,000 dollars.
Every figure on the board comes from a public report, and each step is plain arithmetic, not advice.

visual.label: public numbers · worked out on the board

scenes.say: Here's the recipe we'll repeat at every level. Take gross monthly pay, and set aside 28 percent for housing.
scenes.chapter: The recipe: 28% of pay → a house price

scenes.say: Most of that payment goes to the loan. Freddie Mac's survey put the 30-year fixed rate at 7.21 percent this week.

visual.label: 30-year fixed mortgage rate, week of Nov 25, 2026 (Freddie Mac PMMS)

scenes.say: At 7.21 percent over 30 years, each 100,000 dollars you borrow costs about 679 dollars a month in principal and interest.
Next comes property tax. ATTOM found the average single-family home paid 4,427 dollars in 2025, an effective rate of 0.9 percent.

visual.label: average property tax, single-family home, 2025 (ATTOM) · effective rate 0.9%

scenes.say: Then insurance. NerdWallet puts the average homeowners policy near 2,490 dollars a year, which is about 208 dollars a month.

visual.label: average homeowners insurance per year, $400K dwelling coverage, 2026 (NerdWallet)

scenes.say: And the down payment. In NAR's 2026 buyer profile, first-time buyers put down a median 9 percent, and repeat buyers 19.
The same NAR report found first-time buyers were 22 percent of all buyers, and their typical age stayed at a record 40.
With less than 20 percent down, lenders usually add mortgage insurance, which Freddie Mac says runs 30 to 70 dollars a month per 100,000 borrowed.
Isn't 28 percent too strict? Fannie Mae calls a total debt ratio of 36 percent good, so 28 is the cautious starting line.
Level one is the bottom tenth. In BLS data, one full-time worker in ten earns 634 dollars a week or less.

visual.label: $32,968 · the lowest-paid 10%

scenes.say: Multiply 634 by 52 and you get 32,968 a year, or 2,747 a month. 28 percent of that leaves 769 dollars for housing.
Insurance eats 208 of it. Tax and mortgage insurance take about 92 more, so roughly 470 dollars is left for the loan.
At 7.21 percent, 470 a month carries a loan of about 69,000 dollars, so with 9 percent down the house tops out near 76,000.

visual.label: most house at level 1 (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: Verdict on level one: about 18 percent of the median price. The sign two streets over is more than five times this budget.
Level two is the bottom quarter. A quarter of full-time workers earn 849 dollars a week or less, according to the same BLS table.

visual.label: $44,148 · the lowest-paid 25%

scenes.say: That's 44,148 dollars a year and 3,679 a month, and 28 percent of it gives a housing budget of 1,030 dollars.
After insurance, property tax and mortgage insurance, about 688 dollars a month is left, enough to carry roughly 101,000 dollars of loan.
Put the 9 percent down payment on top, and the ceiling at level two is a house of about 111,000 dollars.

visual.label: most house at level 2 (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: Verdict on level two: about 27 percent of the median house. Climbing from level one bought only 35,000 dollars more.
Level three is the middle, Paula and Sam's salary. Half of full-time workers earn less than 64,064 dollars, and half earn more.

visual.label: $64,064 · the median

scenes.say: The monthly pay is 5,339 dollars, and 28 percent of that is a housing budget of 1,495 dollars every month.
Insurance takes 208, property tax about 131 and mortgage insurance about 79, which leaves 1,077 dollars for principal and interest.
At this week's rate, 1,077 dollars a month carries about 158,600 dollars of loan, so the house tops out near 174,000.

visual.label: most house at level 3, the median salary (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: That's 42 percent of the median price. The distance between this ceiling and the open house sign is about 242,000 dollars.
And even the smaller house needs cash. Nine percent down on 174,242 dollars is 15,682 dollars at closing, before any fees.

visual.label: 9% down payment on the level-3 house

scenes.say: When I first ran this, I expected the median salary to buy something close to the median house. It isn't close at all.
Verdict on level three: at a 7.21 percent rate, the typical paycheck buys well under half of the typical existing home.
If you want to see where the line finally gets crossed, subscribe. Two levels are left, and only one of them clears the sign.
Level four is the top quarter. Three full-time workers in four earn 1,908 dollars a week or less, so this is a strong salary.
1,908 times 52 is 99,216 dollars a year, which is 8,268 a month and a housing budget of 2,315 dollars.
This is close to six figures. After insurance, tax and mortgage insurance, about 1,764 dollars a month goes to the loan itself.
That supports roughly 259,600 dollars of loan and a house of about 285,000, or 69 percent of the median price.

visual.label: most house at level 4 (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: Households often have two earners, so here's that view too. Census put the median household income at 87,460 dollars in 2025.

visual.label: median household income, 2025 (U.S. Census Bureau, P60-289)

scenes.say: Run the median household through the same recipe and the ceiling is about 248,000 dollars, which is 60 percent of the sign.
Verdict on level four: a top-quarter salary covers about two-thirds of the median house, but it still doesn't reach the sign.
Level five is the top tenth. Only one full-time worker in ten earns more than 2,919 dollars a week in the BLS table.
That's 151,788 dollars a year and 12,649 a month, and 28 percent of it is a housing budget of 3,542 dollars.
After 208 for insurance, 338 for tax and 205 for mortgage insurance, about 2,790 dollars a month is left for the loan.
At 7.21 percent that carries about 410,700 dollars of loan, so with 9 percent down the ceiling is close to 451,000 dollars.

visual.label: most house at level 5 (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: Verdict on level five: it's the only level that clears the 416,700 dollar sign, with about 35,000 dollars to spare.
Now run the recipe backwards from the sign. Nine percent down on 416,700 is 37,503 dollars, which leaves a loan of 379,197.
scenes.chapter: The salary the median home needs

scenes.say: That loan costs about 2,577 a month. Add 313 for tax, 190 for mortgage insurance and 208 for insurance, and you reach about 3,286.
Divide that by 28 percent and multiply by 12. The median home needs an income of about 140,800 dollars a year.

visual.label: income needed for the median existing home (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: Redfin's estimate is lower, 109,796 dollars, because it assumes 15 percent down and lets housing take 30 percent of income.
Either way, it's above the top quarter. Two median earners together make 128,128 dollars, and even that couple reaches only 90 percent of the sign.
Wouldn't a lower rate fix it? At 6.21 percent, a full point lower, the median earner's ceiling only rises to about 189,700 dollars.
That's 15,507 dollars more house, because insurance doesn't shrink when rates do, and the gap to the sign was 242,000.
Back to Paula and Sam. They share the same 64,064 dollar salary, but each one has a car payment, and lenders count it.
scenes.chapter: Paula vs Sam: the $27,748 car payment

scenes.say: The total debt line is 36 percent of gross pay. For our median salary, that's 1,922 dollars a month for every debt combined.
Paula pays the average new-car payment, 787 dollars a month. Sam pays the average used-car payment, 582, both from Edmunds.
Subtract the car, and Paula has 1,135 dollars left for housing, while Sam has 1,340. Both are below the 1,495 from the 28 percent rule.
Run the same recipe on those budgets, and Paula's ceiling is about 125,500 dollars, while Sam's is about 153,300.
The difference is 27,748 dollars of house, and it comes from a gap in car payments of just 205 dollars a month.
Couldn't Paula pay the car off first? That's her decision. The math only shows what a monthly payment costs on a mortgage application.
So here's the whole board. Level one buys about 76,000, the median buys about 174,000, and only level five clears 416,700.

visual.label: most house by salary level, $ thousands (28% rule, 7.21%, 9% down)

scenes.say: That's the quiet math of how much house a salary buys: at 7.21 percent, the median home needs a paycheck between the top quarter and the top tenth.
This video explains public data with simple math. It isn't financial advice, and your own rate, state and taxes will be different.

visual.label: not advice

scenes.say: Tell me in the comments: which of the five levels are you on, and how far is the nearest open house sign from your ceiling?
Next on The Quiet Math: your life at every level of net worth, from zero to the top one percent. Subscribe so you don't miss it.

seo.hook: Saturday morning, an open house two streets over: $416,700, the October median. Your paycheck: $1,232 a week. Five real salary levels, one recipe on the board – and only one level reaches the sign.
seo.summary:
How much house can you afford by salary? We take five real pay levels from the Bureau of Labor Statistics – the bottom 10% ($32,968), the bottom 25% ($44,148), the median ($64,064), the top 25% ($99,216) and the top 10% ($151,788) – and run each one through the same recipe on the board: 28% of gross pay, minus insurance, property tax and PMI, at this week's 7.21% mortgage rate (Freddie Mac) with the typical first-time buyer's 9% down payment (NAR 2026).

The result: about $76,000 of house at level 1, $111,000 at level 2, $174,000 at the median, $285,000 at level 4 and $451,000 at level 5 – the only level that clears the October median existing-home price of $416,700 (NAR). Run backwards, the median home needs about $140,800 a year (Redfin's looser assumptions give $109,796). A full point lower rate adds only $15,507 for the median earner. And Payment Paula and Steady Sam, on the same salary, end up $27,748 apart – from a $205 difference in car payments.

HUD Housing Counseling – Study Module 2.1, Housing Affordability (front-end ratio 28%, back-end traditionally 36% for conventional loans)
Fannie Mae – Why Understanding Debt Is Essential (a DTI of 36% or less is considered good)

seo.disclaimer: This video explains public data and simple math for education and entertainment only. It is not financial, mortgage or investment advice. Salary levels are BLS Q3 2026 percentiles of usual weekly earnings for full-time workers (× 52). Each ceiling assumes housing costs of 28% of gross pay, a 30-year fixed loan at Freddie Mac's Nov 25, 2026 average (7.21%), 9% down (NAR 2026 first-time-buyer median), property tax at ATTOM's 0.9% effective rate, $2,490 a year of homeowners insurance (NerdWallet national average for $400K dwelling coverage) and PMI of $50 a month per $100,000 borrowed (middle of Freddie Mac's $30–$70 range). HOA fees, closing costs, credit scores and local prices are excluded. Payment Paula and Steady Sam are illustrative characters on the median salary; their car payments are Edmunds' Q3 2026 averages and the 36% total-debt line is a traditional guideline, not a lender's rule. Your own rate, state, taxes and lender will differ.

forbattring.matt_forra: KLICK_2026-11-26 ~10:20: r5XmMVILOmc 0 visningar på 13 h (för få exponeringar att mäta); eDyeIoffqYw 0 på 34 h. QM-Shorts: Homes 24, Car by Salary 34, 'Fed Disagrees' 0 (just publicerad). Kanalens bästa Short någonsin: gym-psykologin 264.
forbattring.problem: (1) Långa QM-videor får i stort sett inga exponeringar – varken sök eller förslag. (2) 'How broke'-frasen är bred och nyhetsaktig; ingen tydlig sökintention som kopplar till en lösning i videon. (3) Förra videon blev 12:23 mot manusets ≈ 10,6 min – pauserna drar ut. (4) Fem 'quiet numbers' från olika områden gav ingen gemensam tråd att följa.
forbattring.andring: Sökintention med hög volym och tydlig fråga: 'how much house can you afford by salary' (2:a förslaget på 'how much house can you afford', alla 10 följdförslag är lönenivåer). EN tråd genom hela videon: samma recept på tavlan körs på 5 verkliga BLS-percentiler, så tittaren väntar på 'sin' nivå och på vilken nivå som når skylten (bara nivå 5). 1 450 ord ≈ 9,8 min ren röst (kortare än förra 1 557), 69 scener. Beskrivningens kapitel = lönenivåerna, så sökningar 'with 50k/100k/150k salary' hittar rätt kapitel.
forbattring.forvantat: Sökexponeringar inom 48 h på 'how much house can you afford by salary' och 'how much house can i afford with Xk salary', CTR ≥ 4 % efter ≥ 300 exp, ≥ 55 % kvar vid 0:30, ≥ 35 % vid 2:00, snittvisning ≥ 4:00; Shorts ≥ 300 visningar var på 48 h.
forbattring.referens: 'How Are Americans Affording $600,000 Homes on Average Salaries?' – American Finance With Nate, ≈ 588k visningar (FORMAT_BLUEPRINT QM) och '$100K Salary - How Much Can You Afford?' – Jeb Smith, 9 026 visningar på en vecka (Action-trend 23/11, TREND_2026-11-25).
forbattring.vi_slår_den_med: Jeb Smith räknar EN lön; Nate visar hur folk tänjer reglerna. Vi kör samma recept på fem verkliga BLS-percentiler ($32,968–$151,788) med veckans Freddie Mac-ränta (7,21 %), ATTOM-skatt, NerdWallet-försäkring, NAR 2026-insats och PMI – varje rad på tavlan – och svarar baklänges på vad medianhuset kräver ($140,800), varför en lägre ränta knappt hjälper (+$15,507) och vad en bilbetalning kostar i hus (Paula mot Sam $27,748).
forbattring.trend: TREND_2026-11-26.md fanns inte i projektet vid körningen (12:45; LS-körningen skriver den). Egen trendanalys enligt TRENDANALYS.md-reserven: sökförslag hämtade 26/11 ~12:50 – 'how much house can you afford' → 'by salary' (2:a), 'how much house can i afford with 200k/50k/150k/70k salary'; 'how are americans affording' → '$600 000 homes…', '$500 000 homes…', '$100 000 trucks…', 'how broke are americans' (oförändrat 5 dagar). Bevis (Action 23/11 09:25 UTC, TREND_2026-11-25): '$100K Salary - How Much Can You Afford?' (Jeb Smith 9 026/vecka), 'Make $25 an Hour? Here's How Much House You Can Afford' (5 954/vecka), 'Do You Earn Enough To Afford The American Dream in 2026?' (Money Guy 80 323/vecka). Slutsats: lön→hus-frågan har flest specifika förslag i QM-nischen; truck-frasen gjordes 15/11 (MjRogpkdeOA). Sökfras i titeln: 'how much house can you afford by salary'.
